name: Zest
summary: Zero-waste cocktail bar ranked No. 2 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 and Korea's best bar four years running.
description: Zest is the most decorated bar in Korea: No. 2 on Asia's 50 Best Bars for a third straight year and named Best Bar in Korea for the fourth time in 2026. The team works to a zero-waste philosophy, making sodas and spirits in-house and turning leftover peel and pulp into new ingredients. Their gin uses Korean botanicals, and drinks such as the Jeju Garibaldi (hallabong juice with house citrus-peel gin) show off local produce. The ground-floor room on Dosan-daero 55-gil near Apgujeong Rodeo is bright, calm and table-served, so it works better for a group than a counter-only speakeasy.
highlights: Jeju Garibaldi with hallabong juice and house gin
House-made sodas and Korean-botanical gin
Table service with English-speaking staff
tips: Book a few days ahead for a table of 5; weekend evenings fill first. Walk-ins have the best odds at the 18:30 opening.
Opens at 15:00 on Sat and Sun, so an afternoon drink is an easy way to get a table without booking.
TripAdvisor reviewers mention cocktails at around ₩25,000 each. Valet parking is available.
3 min from Apgujeong Rodeo Stn Exit 4 (Suin-Bundang Line), about 25 min from home by taxi.

reviews.text: Reviewers call it a beautiful bar with creative, sustainability-driven drinks, attentive table service and good English.
One visitor found it a calm, sophisticated room rather than a loud party bar, and advised booking a few days ahead.
Naver visitors most often praise the range of drinks (128 mentions), friendly staff and the signature menu.

price.note: Cocktails around ₩25,000 each, as reported by TripAdvisor reviewers

name: Alice Cheongdam
summary: Alice in Wonderland speakeasy behind a flower shop; No. 13 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026, with theatrical cocktails.
description: You enter Alice through a small flower shop at street level, then take a hidden door down into a dim basement lounge. The Alice in Wonderland theme carries through to the drinks, which use molecular techniques and theatrical presentation such as smoke, candy-floss rims and boxed martinis. In 2026 it ranked No. 13 in Asia's 50 Best Bars. Naver marks it as group-friendly with valet parking, so a family table of 5 is realistic if you book.
highlights: Hidden entrance through the flower shop
Theatrical signature cocktails served with smoke and props
Deep whisky list for non-cocktail drinkers
tips: Reserve a table for 5; weekends fill fast. Open until 03:00 on Fri and Sat.
Older TripAdvisor reviews mention a per-person cover charge that includes water and snacks. Expect one to apply.
Rather than ordering five cocktails blind, ask for the signature drinks with the most dramatic presentation. Parents usually enjoy the show.
2 min from Apgujeong Rodeo Stn Exit 3. Valet parking is available.

reviews.text: Reviewers describe an otherworldly entrance and drinks with showpiece presentation, such as cotton-candy rims and smoke-filled skulls.
Bartender skill and friendly service come up again and again, alongside the magical, story-book atmosphere.
Korean visitors highlight the wide drink list, striking interior and unique signature menu.

price.note: Cocktail bar pricing plus a per-person cover charge, as mentioned in TripAdvisor reviews

chuseok.note: Naver Place shows normal hours every day with no Chuseok closure posted. No 2026 notice found; confirm on Instagram before going.

reservation.how: Phone or Instagram DM; walk-ins are possible on weeknights

name: Bar Cham
summary: Hanok cocktail bar in Seochon built on Korean spirits and soju; No. 33 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026.
description: Bar Cham sits in a renovated hanok (traditional house) in Seochon, with oak beams and hand-built furniture. Staff guide you through traditional Korean spirits (jeontongju) from across the country, and the cocktails are built on soju and local liquors. It placed No. 33 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026. The room is calm rather than loud, and it is often cited as one of the most distinctly Korean bars in the city.
highlights: Cocktails built on Korean traditional liquors and soju
Hanok setting with oak interior
Knowledgeable staff who explain each spirit
tips: Party-size rule: TripAdvisor reviewers report a strict maximum of 4 per group, so a family of 5 should split into 2 + 3 or expect to be refused.
Waits are long. Arrive at the 18:00 opening or put your name down early and have dinner nearby in Seochon.
Closed Tuesdays. Pair it with a Gyeongbokgung palace afternoon; it is 6 min from Gyeongbokgung Stn Exit 2 (Line 3, direct from home).

reviews.text: Reviewers praise the original Korean-spirit recipes, fun staff and wonderful vibe, while noting the drinks are a little pricey.
Several reviews criticise the strict four-person limit as rigid, so larger groups have been turned away.
One Naver visitor saw why it made Asia's top 50: very kind staff, Korean-feeling jeontongju cocktails and an oak interior. The only downside was the long wait.

price.note: Signature cocktails; check the menu on Naver Place

hours.note: Closed every Tuesday

name: M+MS
summary: Café by day, experimental fermentation cocktail bar by night; new at No. 42 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026.
description: M+MS is the newcomer of the 2026 list, entering Asia's 50 Best Bars at No. 42. It runs as a café in the afternoon, then turns into a cocktail bar with its own in-house brewing and fermentation programme. The drinks are deliberately experimental; the list's write-up singles out Yama, made with sour kimchi and tuna. Naver reviewers call it the most-talked-about bar in Apgujeong right now, and it has a perfect 5.0 visitor score there.
highlights: In-house brewery and fermentation programme
Experimental signature drinks such as the kimchi-and-tuna Yama
Opens at 14:00, so it works as an afternoon stop
tips: The 14:00 opening makes it one of the few Asia's 50 Best bars you can visit in daylight, which suits parents who prefer an early evening.
No valet parking: use the public lot on Dosan-daero 45-gil. It is 7 min from Apgujeong Rodeo Stn Exit 5.
Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).

reviews.text: Korea Herald notes it works as a café in the afternoon and a cocktail bar in the evening, with an in-house brewery and fermentation programme.
A Naver reviewer calls it the most-watched bar in Apgujeong right now. Very experimental cocktails with a different feel from the other ranked bars.

bestTime: Late afternoon, when it switches from café to bar

name: Gong Gan
summary: Modernised hanok bar near Anguk with a garden courtyard and Korean-inspired cocktails; No. 74 in Asia's 50 Best 2026.
description: Gong Gan occupies a renovated hanok in a quiet alley near Anguk, with about 20 seats around a small central garden. The cocktails lean on Korean ingredients, and sustainability matters here: house-made components and upcycled small bites. It ranked No. 74 on the 2026 Asia's 50 Best Bars 51–100 list. Naver scores it 4.86, one of the highest of any ranked bar, and marks it group-friendly.
highlights: Hanok with a mini garden in the middle
Korean-ingredient signature cocktails
Low-waste snacks and bar food
tips: Opens at 16:00, which makes it an easy post-Bukchon or Changdeokgung drink before dinner.
Closed Mondays and on Chuseok day (25 Sep).
Only about 20 seats, so book on CatchTable for a group of 5.
8 min from Anguk Stn Exit 1 (Line 3, direct from Nambu Bus Terminal, no transfer).

reviews.text: A Naver visitor who went for a second-round whisky found it cosy, modern and beautiful, ideal after dinner near Anguk.
A travel write-up describes the 20-seat hanok with a garden in the middle, blending traditional architecture with Western mixology.

hours.note: Closed Mondays

chuseok.note: Closed on Chuseok day (Fri 25 Sep). Open Thu 24 and Sat 26 Sep. Also closed Mon 28 Sep (weekly day off).

bestTime: From 16:00, after an afternoon in Bukchon

name: Charles H.
summary: Prohibition-style speakeasy hidden in the Four Seasons Seoul basement; No. 87 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026.
description: Charles H. is tucked behind an unmarked door on the lower level of the Four Seasons Hotel Seoul, off Gwanghwamun. It takes its name and spirit from the 1920s travelling bartender Charles H. Baker: a plush Prohibition-era lounge with a menu inspired by his global travels. It rose to No. 87 on the 2026 Asia's 50 Best Bars extended list. Hotel-grade service, sofa seating, valet parking and a group-friendly flag on Naver make it one of the easiest world-class bars for a family of 5.
highlights: Hidden-door entrance inside the Four Seasons
Cocktails inspired by the travels of Charles H. Baker
Pairing of KI ONE Korean whisky with Korean snacks
tips: Ask the Four Seasons front desk how to find the entrance. TripAdvisor reviewers say it is mostly first-come, first-served.
Open daily 17:00–01:30, so it is easy to fit in after a Gyeongbokgung or Gwanghwamun evening walk.
Smart-casual is best; this is a five-star hotel bar.
Gwanghwamun Stn Exit 7 (Line 5) is 2 min away.

reviews.text: Reviewers call it a fun twist on a past era: a hidden Prohibition-style lounge with excellent drinks and confident service.
At least one reviewer was disappointed by the service, so the experience can vary on busy nights.
Korean visitors single out the interior, the range of drinks, the friendly staff and the complimentary snacks.

chuseok.note: Hotel bar open daily 17:00–01:30 per Naver. Hotel bars normally run through Chuseok; no 2026-specific notice found.

name: Le Chamber
summary: Gentlemen's-club speakeasy behind a bookshelf in Cheongdam; No. 88 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 and open till 03:00–04:00.
description: Le Chamber hides behind a bookcase: pull the right book and the wall opens onto a basement lounge of couches, a long marble bar and suited bartenders. It is one of Cheongdam's original high-end speakeasies, with a big whisky and champagne list alongside classic and signature cocktails. It placed No. 88 on the 2026 Asia's 50 Best Bars 51–100 list. It stays open very late, until 04:00 on Fridays and Saturdays.
highlights: The bookshelf door
Deep single-malt and champagne list
Open till 04:00 on Fri and Sat
tips: There is a per-person cover charge, as noted by TripAdvisor reviewers. Weekends are packed.
Book a sofa section for 5 rather than bar seats.
Across the street from Alice, so you can pair the two in one night. 2 min from Apgujeong Rodeo Stn Exit 4.

reviews.text: Reviewers enjoy the bookshelf entrance, the gentlemen's-club couches and the well-dressed staff; many call it a real speakeasy.
Feedback is mixed: one reviewer called it "classy" but "very pricey", and others criticised the service.
Naver visitors praise the wide drink selection, handsome interior and signature menu.

price.note: Premium cocktails plus a per-person cover charge

name: Soko
summary: Underground Hannam bar inspired by 1920s East-meets-West drinking culture; No. 89 in Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026.
description: Soko is a basement bar in Hannam-dong, led by bartender-owner Son Soko and inspired by 1920s drinking culture where East and West met. It pairs a buzzing, clubby energy with precise classics, and serves hearty food such as fried chicken and steak. It has appeared on Asia's 50 Best Bars lists every year since 2023, at No. 89 in 2026. It is less known to tourists than the Cheongdam speakeasies.
highlights: Dry martini
Mr. Peanut: amaro cordial, whisky and peanut
Fried chicken and steak for a proper bar supper
tips: Closed Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep for Chuseok; open again Sat 26.
The substantial bar food makes it a good one-stop late dinner and drinks for a group.
About 14 min walk from Hannam Stn; a taxi from home takes about 15–20 min over Hannam Bridge. Valet parking is available.

reviews.text: World's 50 Best calls it one of Hannam-dong's most elegant secrets, mixing clubby energy with exceptional classic cocktails.
Naver visitors point to the wide drink range, stylish interior and a room that is good for conversation.

name: Bar 81 (Signiel Seoul)
summary: Champagne sky bar on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower: floor-to-ceiling windows over the Han River and all of Seoul.
description: Bar 81 sits inside Signiel Seoul on the 81st floor of Lotte World Tower, Korea's tallest building, so the view out of the full-height windows takes in the Han River bridges on one side and the Jamsil/Gangnam skyline on the other. The room is dark and dramatic, with a double-height ceiling hung with a cloud of glass 'champagne bubbles' and a long marble bar. It is known for one of Asia's largest champagne lists, plus classic and signature cocktails and French-style snack plates (cheese, charcuterie). Forbes Travel Guide named it among the world's best hotel sky bars in 2019. On Friday and Saturday nights a DJ plays, and reviewers report a per-person entrance charge on weekends.
highlights: Window table at sunset, then the lights-on night view (roughly 18:00–20:00 in late September)
Champagne by the glass from a very deep list
Signature cocktails with a cheese or charcuterie plate
Friday–Saturday DJ set 21:30–23:15 (per a Jan 2026 visitor report)
tips: Book a window table in advance (CatchTable or +82-2-3213-1281); a Jan 2026 visitor says window seats are fought over and weekend walk-ins are hard. Online booking slots run 17:00–21:00.

Money flags: a Jan 2026 blog reports a weekend entrance charge of about ₩31,000 per person, and one TripAdvisor reviewer (Oct 2023) says staff asked every member of their group to order. Assume everyone orders at least one drink.
Dress smart casual (no gym wear or flip-flops). The bar has its own smoking room, so the main room stays smoke-free.
Enter at the Signiel lobby entrance at the base of Lotte World Tower (not the Seoul Sky observatory queue) and take the hotel lift up. Pair it with dinner in Lotte World Mall below.

name: The Timber House (Park Hyatt Seoul)
nameKo: 파크 하얏트 서울 더 팀버 하우스
subcategory: Hotel whisky & cocktail bar with live music
summary: Park Hyatt's basement vinyl-and-whisky bar: Korean-accented cocktails, sushi plates and live jazz or soul sets most nights.
description: The Timber House is in the lower level of Park Hyatt Seoul, directly above Samseong Station. After a renovation it reopened as a vinyl music bar with wood, stone and brick rooms, walls of records, a grand piano and a small stage, split into several intimate seating areas. Drinks focus on premium whisky and signature cocktails that use Korean ingredients. The kitchen does Japanese izakaya plates, sashimi and a sushi omakase. The venue's Naver notice lists live sets every night from 20:30 through September 2026. There is no view here: it is a moody, windowless room, which makes it a good pick for a rainy night.
highlights: Live sets from 20:30 nightly (2 sets Mon–Tue, 3 sets later in the week, per the venue's September 2026 notice)
Groove Hour 17:00–19:00: signature drinks and bites at 50% off (reported 2025)
Signature cocktails such as Heart & Seoul and the Park Hyatt Negroni (about ₩32,000–33,000)
Johnnie Walker Blue pairing (cocktail, neat pour and chocolate) for ₩120,000, 1 Sep–31 Oct 2026
tips: Arrive at 17:00 for the half-price Groove Hour, eat, then stay for the 20:30 set. This is the value play in an expensive hotel bar.
DiningCode reviewers report a music charge of about ₩10,000 per person during evening performances. Confirm when booking (+82-2-2016-1235).
For 5 people, reserve a table rather than the counter. Naver marks the venue as a no-kids zone, which is not an issue for an adult group.
Take Samseong Station (Line 2) Exit 1; the hotel entrance is right at the exit. Per Naver, valet parking is free and self-parking costs ₩10,000 for the first 3 hours.

reviews.text: This bar has great ambiance. The cocktails are exquisite.
reviews.author: Brent H

reviews.text: The staff is warm and engaging and make you feel so welcome.
reviews.author: philip r

reviews.text: Naver visitors most often vote for kind staff, good food, the interior, a wide drinks list and good music.
Korean reviewers describe a speakeasy-like hidden entrance and short acoustic sets, such as electric violin and jazz vocals, that suit anniversaries or quiet catch-ups.

price.note: Signature cocktails about ₩32,000–33,000 (DiningCode menu listing). Snack and share plates ₩99,000–100,000; signature dinner course ₩169,000. A music charge of about ₩10,000 pp is reported during live sets.

hours.note: Naver lists 17:00–24:00 daily. DiningCode shows Sunday 15:00–22:00, so check Sunday hours. September 2026 live sets: Mon–Tue 20:30 and 21:30; later in the week an extra 22:30 set.

chuseok.note: No specific Chuseok notice found. The venue's Naver notices run a September 2026 live-music schedule for the whole month and a Johnnie Walker Blue promotion from 1 Sep to 31 Oct, with no holiday closure mentioned. Hotel bars normally operate through Chuseok.

name: MOBO Bar (JW Marriott Hotel Seoul)
subcategory: Hotel botanical cocktail bar with garden terrace
summary: A 'modern botanical' cocktail bar on JW Marriott Banpo's 7th floor, with its own greenhouse and garden terrace, two Line 3 stops from home.
description: MOBO (short for 'modern botanical') is on the 7th floor of JW Marriott Hotel Seoul, above Express Bus Terminal and the Shinsegae Gangnam complex. A long dark-wood bar faces a wall of grow-lit shelves. Behind it are a glass greenhouse where the team grows herbs and fruit for the drinks, and an open-air garden terrace with sofas. The cocktail list is built around five themes (Tonic, Fruits, Herbs, Spices and Earth). In 2025 Forbes Travel Guide put it on its 58 Star Bars list, the only bar in Korea to make it. It is TripAdvisor's top-rated hotel bar in this group and the closest to home.
highlights: Garden terrace on a mild late-September evening
Herb-forward signature cocktails such as Herb of Grace (₩29,000) and San Martini (₩38,000)
Greenhouse-and-grow-wall interior
Forbes Travel Guide 2025 Star Bar (only one in Korea)
tips: The easiest nightcap from home: two stops on Line 3 to Express Bus Terminal, or a short taxi. It stays open until 02:00 on Friday and Saturday.
Ask for the outdoor terrace sofas for 5. Naver reviewers single out the outdoor space (야외공간이 멋져요), and the terrace suits parents better than bar stools.
Marriott's listing marks it as not taking reservations, so arrive early on Friday and Saturday or phone +82-2-6282-6739 to check.
Hotel parking at JW Marriott is free for 5 hours, per Naver.

reviews.text: Cozy bar with good food & drinks and, above all, great service.
reviews.author: Peter

reviews.text: The atmosphere is very good and the cocktails are fresh and delicious.
Korean visitors praise the outdoor terrace atmosphere, the bartenders' skill and the service, while noting that prices are hotel-level.
On Naver, visitors most often vote for tasty food, kind staff, a wide drinks list, the interior and the outdoor space.

name: Euljiro Nogari Alley (Manseon Hof)
summary: Legendary Euljiro alley of plastic tables, cheap draft beer and grilled nogari (dried pollack), anchored by Manseon Hof since 1980.
description: Around Euljiro 3-ga's printing-shop lanes, hofs spill hundreds of plastic tables onto the street every evening. Crowds drink cold draft beer here with grilled nogari (dried young pollack) dipped in spicy sauce and mayo. Manseon Hof, running since 1980, started the trend and now spreads across several buildings, including rooftop sections. It is the most 'real Seoul' night out on this list: loud, cheap, very Korean, and easy for a group of 5 to grab a table. Naver reviewers rate it highly for value (394 mentions) and for group gatherings.
highlights: Grilled nogari with spicy mayo dip
Golbaengi muchim (spicy sea-snail salad with noodles)
Garlic fried chicken
Outdoor street tables on warm September evenings
tips: Go 18:00–19:00 to get an outdoor table before the after-work crowd; by 20:00 on Thu–Fri the alley is packed.
Order a round of draft beer and nogari first, since both come fast and cheap, then add chicken or golbaengi.
Rain plan: Manseon Hof spreads over several buildings with indoor seating, so the night still works.
Euljiro 3-ga Stn Exit 4 (Line 2/3) is 3 min away. It is a direct Line 3 ride from Nambu Bus Terminal.

reviews.text: Naver visitors praise the food, the value for money (394 mentions) and how good it is for group gatherings.
10 Magazine calls Manseon Hof the anchor of Euljiro's hidden pocha street, where hofs spill plastic tables into the lanes.
Trip.com travellers describe a massive, multi-building pub with rooftop zones, where cold beer and garlic chicken are the stars.

price.note: Among the cheapest nights out in central Seoul: draft beer plus shared snacks

hours.note: Hours shown are Manseon Hof's (per Naver). Other alley hofs vary; most open from late afternoon.

chuseok.note: Manseon Hof lists daily hours on Naver with no Chuseok closure posted, but no 2026 notice was found. Smaller alley hofs often close on Chuseok day. Safest days are 23 Sep and 27–30 Sep.

name: Saeseoul
summary: Pink building with a retro arcade downstairs, a Korean-twist cocktail bar and a rooftop over the Jongno 3-ga hanok roofs.
description: Saeseoul stacks a retro game arcade on the lower floors, a cocktail bar on the third and a rooftop terrace looking over the low hanok roofs of Ikseon-dong and Jongno. Cocktails come with alcohol, sweetness and acidity ratings on the menu, and several are named after arcade games, such as Pac-Man. It sits right at the mouth of the Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha street, where orange-tented street stalls set up every evening. With over 5,600 Naver visitor reviews, it is hugely popular with young Seoulites but rarely on tourist lists.
highlights: Rooftop views over Ikseon-dong hanok roofs
Pac-Man and other arcade-themed cocktails
Retro arcade games on the way up
Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha tent street right outside
tips: Naver lists it as a no-kids zone, which is fine for adults. Book the rooftop for groups on Naver.
Blankets are provided on cool evenings, and late-September nights can be chilly up top.
Combine it with the orange-tent pojangmacha stalls on the street outside for an easy two-stop night.
Jongno 3-ga Stn Exit 4 is 2 min away. Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).

reviews.text: Over 2,700 Naver visitors single out the view, alongside the drink range and good food.
Travellers note you walk through the arcade and up several floors to find it; the vibe shifts from relaxed afternoon to DJ-led lounge at night.

chuseok.note: Closed on Chuseok day (Fri 25 Sep); open 24 and 26 Sep with normal hours.

name: Dameun (Express Bus Terminal)
summary: Near-home jeon-and-traditional-liquor pub under Banpo Shopping Town: Korean pancakes, makgeolli and a big sool list.
description: Dameun is a basement yori-jujeom (Korean gastro-pub) in Banpo Shopping Town, right at Express Bus Terminal Station. It is one Line 3 stop from home. The draw is a wide list of Korean traditional liquors and makgeolli, paired with platters of jeon (savoury pancakes), yukjeon (beef jeon) and seafood dishes. Locals love it: Naver visitors mostly praise the food (334 mentions) and the drink range (252). It has group seating, a waiting area and reservations, making it an easy, low-stress night out for a family of 5.
highlights: Moduem-jeon (assorted pancake platter)
Yukjeon (pan-fried beef slices)
Wide selection of makgeolli and Korean traditional liquors
Pohang octopus sashimi
tips: Holiday hours posted on Naver: 15:00–23:00 every day from 24 to 27 Sep, so it is one of the few local pubs open on Chuseok day.
Use Exit 8-1 or 8-2 at Express Bus Terminal Stn and take the stairs down to B1 of Banpo Shopping Town, building 4.
From home it is 2 stops on Line 3 (Nambu Bus Terminal → Express Bus Terminal), or a very short taxi ride.
Reservations are accepted; book a table for 5 on Fri and Sat nights.

reviews.text: Naver visitors mostly praise the tasty food and the wide choice of drinks, plus kind staff and good complimentary side dishes.
Reviewers flag the jeon platters and traditional-liquor list as the reasons to come back.

price.note: Shared jeon platters plus bottles of makgeolli and traditional liquor

hours.note: Chuseok week (24–27 Sep) hours are 15:00–23:00 daily. Regular Thu–Sun hours are not shown this week.

chuseok.note: Open throughout Chuseok with holiday hours of 15:00–23:00 on 24, 25, 26 and 27 Sep, as posted on Naver Place.

location.address: B1, Banpo Shopping Town Bldg 4, 189 Sinbanpo-ro, Seocho-gu, Seoul

bestTime: Any evening; open on Chuseok day

name: Hanchu
summary: Two-decade-old Sinsa-dong chimaek hof, famous for double-fried chicken and crispy fried chilli peppers with cold beer.
description: Hanchu is a single-location hof near Garosu-gil that has fried chicken for over 20 years; it is not a franchise. Regulars come for double-fried chicken tossed with chilli, pork-stuffed fried green peppers, and pitchers of ice-cold beer. Naver lists over 1,600 visitor reviews, most praising the food, and marks it as good for group gatherings (203 mentions). TripAdvisor opinion is split: some visitors love the crunch, while others find the chicken dry. Treat it as a lively local chimaek night, not a gastronomic event.
highlights: Double-fried chicken with chilli
Gochu twigim: pork-stuffed fried peppers
Ice-cold draft beer
tips: Closed 24–26 Sep for Chuseok and every Sunday. For the family, the best nights are Mon 28–Wed 30 Sep.
Opens at 14:00, so a late-afternoon chimaek after Garosu-gil shopping beats the evening queue.
Share a couple of chicken orders among 5, plus a plate of the stuffed peppers.
9 min from Apgujeong Stn Exit 5 (Line 3, direct from home) or a short taxi from Sinsa.

reviews.text: Naver visitors overwhelmingly praise the food (811 mentions) and say it is great for group gatherings.
Mixed: some reviewers praise the chicken, ice-cold beer and helpful staff, while one called the chicken dry and the service poor.
Food blogger Daniel Food Diary highlights the fried chilli peppers and the non-franchise, one-location heritage.

hours.note: Closed Sundays. Thu–Sat regular hours are not shown this week because of the Chuseok closure; Naver notes last order is 1 h before close on Fri and Sat.

chuseok.note: Closed Thu 24 – Sat 26 Sep for Chuseok, and also closed Sun 27 (regular Sunday closure). Reopens Mon 28 Sep at 14:00.

name: Haneum Seongsu
summary: Seongsu gastro-pub pairing Korea's traditional liquors with modern anju such as octopus bossam and beef tartare.
description: Haneum is a modern yori-jujeom a minute from Ttukseom Station, popular with Seongsu's young crowd for its menu of Korean traditional liquors. The anju (drinking food) is serious: garlic octopus bossam, sushi-style hot pots, yukhoe (beef tartare) and seafood-and-chive jeon. It has over 1,200 Naver visitor reviews, with more than a thousand praising the food and 552 the drink range. It accepts reservations and group tables, so it is a comfortable way for parents to try sool beyond soju.
highlights: Munuh-maneul bossam (octopus and garlic bossam)
Yukhoe (Korean beef tartare)
Curated Korean traditional liquor list
tips: Closed Sat 26 Sep (Chuseok) and every Sunday. Open 24 and 25 Sep.
Pair it with an afternoon at Seoul Forest or the Seongsu pop-ups; Ttukseom Stn Exit 7 or 8 is 1–2 min away.
Ask staff for a tasting-style mix of takju (makgeolli) and yakju (clear rice wine) to share among 5.

reviews.text: Naver visitors overwhelmingly praise the food (1,104 mentions) and the drink variety, and say the room is good for conversation.
Reviewers also mention generous complimentary side dishes and an attractive interior.

hours.note: Closed Sundays

chuseok.note: Open Thu 24 and Fri 25 Sep (17:00–02:00); closed Sat 26 Sep for Chuseok and Sun 27 (regular day off).

name: All That Jazz
summary: Korea's oldest jazz club (since 1976), now in a dramatic all-red Itaewon room with live bands every night of the week.
description: All That Jazz opened in Itaewon in 1976 and is the country's oldest active jazz club; in 2023 it moved into a 275 m² second-floor space on Itaewon-ro designed by studio mttb, reached through a red door and a neon-lit corridor. The room is wrapped in red curtains and banquettes, with a long bar and a proper stage for piano, horns and big bands. There are two sets on weeknights (19:00–20:00 and 20:30–23:00) and three on Fridays and Saturdays, the last running until 02:50. The music charge is ₩15,000 per person per set, paid on the night, on top of cocktails, wine and plates.
highlights: Live jazz 364 days a year, with a new line-up nightly
Red, cinematic 2023 interior by mttb, with a long cocktail bar
Fri/Sat three-set nights; bands and quintets in the early set
Window seats overlooking Itaewon-ro
tips: Cover is ₩15,000 per person per set (two sets = ₩30,000); it is charged on the night, not when you book.
For 5 people incl. parents, book a table in advance on the club's website or Kakao channel and go for the 19:00 or 20:30 set; weeknights are calmer and walk-ins usually work for couples.
Naver reviewers suggest window seats, and eating dinner elsewhere first — drinks are the strength here.
No building parking; valet is reported at the nearby IBK bank branch. Itaewon Stn (Line 6) Exit 3 is about a 6-minute walk.

reviews.text: Excellent music, great food, nice staff, easy to get to.
reviews.author: Melbontour

reviews.text: We went without a reservation and they welcomed us with a smile and made us sit near the stage.
reviews.author: Micol

reviews.text: A long-time fan finally visited with their adult son after the move and loved hearing a top quintet up close in such an atmospheric room (translated).
The new space feels far more comfortable than the old one; on a weekday you can likely get in without booking (translated).

price.note: Music charge ₩15,000 per person per set (Naver menu); cocktails listed around ₩25,000 and fish & chips ₩30,000 (DiningCode).

hours.note: Sets: 19:00–20:00 and 20:30–23:00 Sun–Thu; Fri/Sat 19:00–21:30, 22:00–00:30 and 00:30–02:50 (official online schedule). Naver lists 18:00–24:00 daily, so confirm late closing on Fri/Sat.

chuseok.note: Open all three Chuseok days: Naver Place lists 18:00–24:00 hours for 24, 25 and 26 Sep marked 추석 연휴, and the club's schedule has bands booked each night (three sets on Fri 25 and Sat 26).

name: Club Evans
summary: Hongdae's 25-year-old jazz club: two live sets nightly a few steps from the stage, for about ₩15,000–20,000 entry.
description: Club Evans, named after pianist Bill Evans, has been the home stage of Korea's young jazz scene near Hongik University since 2001 and runs its own label. There is no barrier between stage and tables, so you sit a few metres from the players. Doors open at 19:00, the first set runs 20:00–20:50 and the second 21:20–22:10, with a different band every night and open jam sessions on Mondays and Tuesdays. Entry is ₩15,000 Sunday–Friday and ₩20,000 on Saturday, plus one drink per person; cocktails and beer are simple and inexpensive.
highlights: A different Korean jazz band every night, often the scene's best young players
Open jam nights on Mondays ('Super Jam Day') and Tuesdays ('Urban Jam Day')
Intimate room with no barrier between stage and tables
Blue Lagoon and other classic cocktails at bar-snack prices
tips: No reservations — seats are first come, first served. On weekends a queue forms, so arrive at 19:00 when doors open if you want a table for 5; back rows are cramped.
Budget ₩15,000 entry (₩20,000 on Saturday) plus one compulsory drink each; the fee can change for special shows.
It is a small, second-floor room (entrance to the right of the 7-Eleven, 150 m from Sangsu Stn Exit 1). Parents who dislike tight seating may prefer All That Jazz.
Under-19s are admitted only with a legal guardian.

reviews.text: A serious Jazzclub with a great schedule.
Weekend queues are long so go early and line up; the playing was superb, though the back-row seats were not comfortable and drinks came slowly (translated).
Second visit after last year — the cocktails are good every time and the owner makes great shows easy to discover (translated).

price.note: Entry ₩15,000 Sun–Fri, ₩20,000 Sat (club FAQ, as of Jan 2025) plus one drink each; drinks about ₩8,000–12,000 (DiningCode).

hours.note: Doors 19:00; sets 20:00–20:50 and 21:20–22:10. Mondays and Tuesdays are jam-session nights.

chuseok.note: The club's September 2026 calendar marks Thu 24 Sep as closed (휴무); bands are booked on Fri 25 (Christian Alte Quartet) and Sat 26 (ROBIQ'S WORLD).

name: Jusindang (Zoo Sindang) Gangnam
summary: Shaman-shrine themed bar with a cocktail for each of the 12 Korean zodiac animals, 3 min from Gangnam Station.
description: Jusindang (酒神堂, 'house of the god of drink') turns Korean shamanic imagery into a moody, design-forward bar. The menu has one cocktail for each of the 12 zodiac animals (rat, ox, tiger and so on), so each family member can order their own birth-year drink. Unlike most cocktail bars, the Gangnam branch runs a proper Korean-modern kitchen: grilled hanwoo steak, sous-vide beef short rib, spicy fish stew and potato jeon. With 9,500 Naver visitor reviews, it is a Seoul favourite with locals yet little known to tourists.
highlights: Your own zodiac-animal cocktail (₩17,000–19,000)
Sous-vide beef short rib (₩45,000)
Potato jeon and gondre noodles for sharing
Lunch and evening set courses from ₩18,000
tips: Look up each person's Korean zodiac animal by birth year before you go; it is a fun ritual to order by sign.
Opens 11:00 with a 15:00–17:00 break, so a lunch course here is an easy daytime taste of the concept for parents.
Naver lists reservations and a high chair for this branch. Book for 5 on weekends, when the Gangnam queue gets long.
Gangnam Stn Exit 11 (Line 2 / Shinbundang), 3 min walk. It is 2 stops from Gyodae on Line 2.

reviews.text: Naver visitors praise the food (7,812 mentions) as much as the drinks, and 5,665 highlight the striking interior.
The Smart Local describes a hidden oriental bar where you order a cocktail matched to your zodiac sign, entered past a stone guardian statue.
A 2025 review calls it part bar, part themed experience: modern design built around a contemporary take on Korean shamanism.

hours.note: Daily, with a break from 15:00 to 17:00

chuseok.note: Naver lists it as open daily with no Chuseok closure posted, but no 2026 notice was found. Chuseok day (25 Sep) is uncertain; call ahead.

images.alt: Grilled hanwoo steak with eohyang sauce

name: Bar Guilty
summary: Quiet classic-cocktail bar between Seocho and Gyodae stations, about a 10-min walk from home; open until 03:00 nightly.
description: Bar Guilty is a small ground-floor cocktail bar tucked into the legal-district streets between Seocho and Gyodae stations. It serves carefully made classics and house signatures such as the Prohibition, Flower Garden, Mai Tai and Bloody Mary. Almost no tourists find it: it has only a few dozen Naver reviews, but they consistently praise the drink range, kind bartenders and a room quiet enough to talk. It is the easiest nightcap on the list, close enough to walk home.
highlights: Prohibition (house signature, ₩25,000)
Old Fashioned and Espresso Martini
Quiet room built for conversation
tips: Closest bar to home on this list: about 10 min on foot (Seocho Stn Exit 1, Gyodae Exit 14 or Nambu Bus Terminal Exit 6).
Open daily until 03:00 (last order 02:30), so it works as a late nightcap after dinner anywhere in the city.
Naver marks it group-friendly and takes reservations; call ahead to hold a table for 5.

reviews.text: Naver visitors mostly mention the wide drink selection, friendly staff and a relaxed room that is good for conversation.
Reviewers also like the interior and the complimentary bar snacks.

chuseok.note: Naver lists daily hours with no Chuseok closure posted, but no 2026 notice was found. Chuseok day is uncertain; call +82-2-588-3408.

name: Saloon 4350
summary: Two-floor dining pub near Gyodae with a huge sound system, draught Guinness, whisky highballs and hearty plates.
description: Saloon 4350 bills itself as a luxury dining pub with an 'overwhelming' speaker system, and music is part of the draw: Naver reviewers single out the sound (185 mentions). It spreads over two floors on Seocho-daero 46-gil, 3 min from Gyodae, so a group of 5 can sprawl. The menu covers draught Guinness and Stella, craft pale ale, highballs from Kakubin to Hakushu, bottles of wine and single malts. The food is substantial: Chicago-style pizza, a sirloin steak with ghee butter, gambas and golbaengi.
highlights: Guinness on draught (₩11,000)
Whisky highballs from ₩9,000
Chicago meat pizza and ghee-butter sirloin
Big-speaker sound system
tips: Closed Sundays and on Chuseok day (25 Sep); open 24 and 26 Sep.
5 min from Gyodae Stn Exit 14, and easily walkable from home.
Good pick when parents want food and a drink rather than a cocktail bar; plates run ₩13,000–49,000.

reviews.text: Naver visitors praise the food (356 mentions), the interior and especially the music and sound system.
Reviewers also call it spacious with friendly service, an easy place for a group.

hours.note: Closed Sundays. Regular Friday hours are not shown this week because of the Chuseok closure.

chuseok.note: Closed on Chuseok day (Fri 25 Sep) and Sun 27 (weekly day off). Open Thu 24 and Sat 26 Sep, 17:00–24:00.

name: Kkokkio Firewood Chicken
summary: Two-floor Gangnam pub for firewood-roasted chicken, golbaengi and nogari with soju or beer; open until 03:30.
description: Kkokkio is a big, busy Gangnam Station pub built around whole chicken roasted over firewood. The house special is hanbang nurungji tongdak: herbal chicken on crispy scorched rice. Around it sit the classic Korean drinking anju: spicy golbaengi with noodles, fire-grilled boneless chicken feet, nogari and meoktae (dried pollack), and pojangmacha udon. At ₩19,900 for the signature chicken, it is solid value for Gangnam. Naver visitors praise the food (1,222 mentions) and the roomy two floors (527).
highlights: Hanbang nurungji tongdak (herbal chicken on crispy rice, ₩19,900)
Golbaengi somyeon (spicy sea snails with noodles)
Nogari and meoktae with mayo dip
tips: Open daily 16:00–03:30 (last order 02:30), so it is a safe late-night fallback.
Two floors with group tables; Naver also lists high chairs.
5 min from Gangnam Stn Exit 3.

reviews.text: Naver visitors mostly praise the food, how spacious it is and the fresh ingredients.
Reviewers point to the signature scorched-rice roast chicken as the reason to go.

chuseok.note: Naver lists it as open daily with no Chuseok closure posted, but no 2026 notice was found. Chuseok day is uncertain.

name: Birdman
summary: Quirky bird-themed basement speakeasy off Garosu-gil, with spirit-forward cocktails and vintage curios.
description: Birdman hides in a basement just off Garosu-gil, greeting guests with a red bird under a glass cloche. Inside it is dark and a little eccentric, with murals, vintage trinkets and good music. The cocktail list is spirit-forward, with classics like the Penicillin and Old Fashioned alongside signatures from about ₩17,000. It is a hidden gem even for locals and an easy extension of a Sinsa shopping day, with 671 Naver blog reviews.
highlights: Signature cocktails from about ₩17,000
Penicillin and Old Fashioned
Eccentric vintage bird-themed decor
tips: Book ahead; the small room fills quickly, and a group of 5 needs a reserved table.
Open daily from 19:00 until 02:30, or 03:30 on Fri and Sat.
10 min walk from Sinsa Stn Exit 8 or Apgujeong Stn Exit 4 (Line 3, direct from home).

reviews.text: Clumsy Girl Travels describes a dark, quirky, slightly creepy room of murals and vintage trinkets, with chill vibes and a great cocktail menu.
Naver visitors highlight the interior first (83 mentions), then the drink range and the food.

chuseok.note: Naver shows normal daily hours with no Chuseok closure posted, but no 2026 notice was found. Chuseok day is uncertain.

name: The Paris Bar (Grand Hyatt Seoul)
summary: Grand Hyatt's French-styled bar on Namsan, with live jazz, signature cocktails and Seoul city lights beyond the windows.
description: The Paris Bar sits below the lobby of the Grand Hyatt Seoul, high on the slope of Namsan. The hotel describes live jazz performances with the city lights of Seoul visible indoors or out. The room is discreet and stylish with French touches, and pairs signature cocktails with French-inspired snacks. For parents it is the most classic, comfortable way to enjoy a night view: armchairs, valet parking and five-star service.
highlights: Live jazz sets in the evening
City-light views from the Namsan hillside
Signature cocktails and French-inspired bar snacks
tips: Closed every Tuesday (29 Sep). Open 18:00–01:00 on other nights, last order 00:00.
Reserve a window table on TableCheck.
No subway nearby (Hannam-jin Stn is a 20-min uphill walk). Take a taxi, or use valet if driving.

reviews.text: Naver visitors mostly praise the music, kind staff, drink range and a clean, stylish room.
Hotel listings describe a classy, discreet bar with French elements and spectacular views of the capital.

hours.note: Closed Tuesdays

chuseok.note: Naver shows normal hours for 24–26 Sep with no holiday closure, and hotel bars normally run through Chuseok. No 2026 notice found. Closed Tue 29 Sep (weekly).

name: Southside Parlor
subcategory: Cocktail bar & Texas BBQ with rooftop
summary: Itaewon favourite for fresh-juice craft cocktails, Texas BBQ and southern hospitality, with a 4th-floor rooftop.
description: Southside Parlor has been a Seoul cocktail institution for more than a decade, founded to bring craft cocktails, Texas BBQ and southern hospitality to Itaewon. Every juice is fresh-squeezed and every syrup house-made, and the kitchen turns out burgers, brisket, tacos and wings that make it a full dinner stop. In good weather the 4th-floor rooftop opens over Noksapyeong-daero. It is rated 4.6 on TripAdvisor (#184 in Seoul). English is the house language, so it is the most relaxed choice on this list for parents.
highlights: Signature seasonal cocktails with fresh juices and house syrups
Burgers, brisket and fish tacos
Rooftop terrace on the 4th floor
tips: Closed Mondays (28 Sep). Opens 17:00 on Sat and Sun, 18:00 on weekdays.
Ask for the rooftop when booking; it depends on the weather.
Noksapyeong Stn Exit 2 (Line 6) is 6 min away. From home, take a taxi (about 20 min) or change to Line 6 at Samgakji.

reviews.text: Reviewers praise the fresh-squeezed juices and house syrups, calling them the best cocktails in Seoul, in a down-to-earth atmosphere.
One reviewer rated the burger "Best Burger Ever" and worked through the entire signature cocktail list.
Korean visitors rate the food highest (346 mentions), then the drink range and the interior.

hours.note: Closed Mondays

chuseok.note: Naver shows normal hours for 24–26 Sep with no holiday closure posted, but there is no explicit 2026 notice, so confirm on Instagram. Closed Mon 28 Sep (weekly).

name: Pyeonggyunyul
summary: Dimly lit Euljiro LP bar with shelves of vinyl, wine and whisky; request a record from the jazz-heavy collection.
description: Pyeonggyunyul is a dim second-floor LP bar right by Euljiro 3-ga Station. Walls of vinyl surround the room, and staff spin jazz and classics, taking song requests (Chet Baker is a house favourite). Guests come for wine and whisky rather than cocktails, and for the romance of the room. Naver visitors rate the music first (185 mentions), then the interior; its 893 blog reviews make it one of the best-known LP bars among young Koreans.
highlights: Wall-to-wall vinyl collection
Song requests
Wine and whisky by the glass
tips: Naver lists it as a no-kids zone, so it is adults only. The room is intimate, so a group of 5 should book.
Opens 13:00 on Saturdays (break 17:00–18:00) and 14:00 on Sundays, making it a great rainy-afternoon stop.
Euljiro 3-ga Stn Exit 8 is directly below (Line 3 from home). Closed on Chuseok day (25 Sep).

reviews.text: Trazy describes a jazzy LP bar where you drink whisky or wine beside shelves of records and can request songs.
Budify calls it a place of darkness and romance: a wine LP bar that turns nostalgic tracks and good wine into joy.
Naver visitors most often praise the music and the atmospheric interior.

price.note: Wine by the glass or bottle, plus whisky

hours.note: Regular Friday hours are not shown this week because of the Chuseok closure.

name: Koya Record
summary: Euljiro back-alley music bar loved for its vinyl sound, drinks and food; opens at noon on weekends.
description: Koya Record hides in the back lane behind J-Macro Tower in Euljiro, reached through a side door by a real-estate office sign. It is a record-driven music bar: over 700 Naver visitors single out the music, and nearly as many praise the drinks, interior and food. It is larger than most LP bars, marked group-friendly and bookable, so it suits a group of 5. From Friday to Sunday it opens at noon, which is rare for a music bar.
highlights: Vinyl-driven music programme
Food menu that works as dinner
Weekend daytime opening from 12:00
tips: Naver lists it as a no-kids zone, so it is adults only. Book a table for 5 on Naver.
Finding it: go to the back alley of J-Macro Tower 1F and enter via the door to the right of the real-estate sign.
Pairs well with Euljiro nogari alley (5 min away) for a two-stop Euljiro night.

reviews.text: Naver visitors praise the music most (710 mentions), closely followed by the drink list, interior and food.
Many also note it is a good place for conversation despite the music focus.

name: Mood Seoul (Some Sevit)
summary: Wine bar on Some Sevit's floating Solbit island, near home, with Han River night views by Banpo Bridge.
description: Mood Seoul occupies Solbit, one of the Some Sevit floating islands on the Han River beside Banpo Bridge. It is the closest real riverside night-view bar to home. The wine list comes with a full kitchen; the signature is pomodoro pasta topped with lobster, snow crab, octopus, abalone and shrimp. Naver visitors rate the interior highest (377 mentions), then the food. With the water all around and the city lit up across the river, it is a comfortable, parent-friendly way to do 'Seoul at night'.
highlights: Han River and Banpo Bridge views from a floating island
Signature seafood pomodoro pasta
Wine by the glass and bottle
tips: Closed Thu 24 Sep for Chuseok; open 25 and 26 Sep. Weekday kitchen closes early (last order 20:30), so book 18:00–19:00.
Getting there: Express Bus Terminal Stn Exit 4 then bus 740 one stop, or a 20-min walk from Exit 8-1. A taxi from home is quickest.
Walk the Banpo Hangang Park riverside afterwards; the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain is on Banpo Bridge right next door (check the day's show times).

reviews.text: Naver visitors rate the interior and setting highest, followed by the food and friendly service.
The seafood pomodoro pasta with lobster and snow crab is the dish most visitors order.

price.note: Wine and dining; seafood pasta is the signature

chuseok.note: Closed Thu 24 Sep (Chuseok, per Naver notice). Open on Chuseok day (25 Sep) and 26 Sep.

name: Monday Blues
summary: Seocho-side wine bistro near Gangnam Station: 72-hour pork belly, sirloin steak and paella with a friendly wine list.
description: Monday Blues is a wine bar and bistro on the Seocho side of Gangnam Station, in the lobby of the Samsung Chervill building. It is serious about food: 72-hour slow-cooked pork belly, sirloin steak, crab rosé pasta and squid-ink paella, all built for sharing with a bottle. Naver visitors praise the food first (646 mentions) and the interior second, with 1,155 blog reviews. It opens at 11:00 for lunch, which makes an early family dinner easy, and it is about 15 minutes from home.
highlights: 72-hour slow-cooked pork belly
Sirloin steak
Squid-ink paella
Crab rosé pasta

name: Magpie Brewshop Itaewon
summary: Original taproom of Magpie, the Itaewon brewery that helped start Korea's craft-beer boom, pouring fresh Jeju-brewed drafts.
description: Magpie Brewing was founded in Itaewon's Gyeongnidan in 2012 by four beer-loving friends and helped spark Korea's craft-beer revolution. The Brewshop keeps the original concept: just great beer, with fresh drafts shipped from Magpie's brewery on Jeju. There is no kitchen, but you can bring food or order delivery. It is small and casual, rated 4.5 on TripAdvisor, and good value for a beer-lover's hour before dinner in Itaewon or Haebangchon.
highlights: Magpie Pale Ale, Porter and IPA on draft
Seasonal Jeju-brewed specials
Bring-your-own-food policy
tips: Open Wed–Sun 17:00–23:00 only; closed Mon, Tue and Chuseok day (25 Sep).
The entrance is in the first alley on the left off the main road.
Small room: treat it as a first-round beer, then move on to dinner.

reviews.text: Reviewers call it a craft-beer pioneer with excellent fresh drafts and a friendly, low-key crowd.
Naver visitors mention the beer variety and that it is an easy place to drink solo.

price.note: Draft craft beer; no food served

hours.note: Closed Mondays and Tuesdays

name: Privilege Bar (Mondrian Seoul Itaewon)
summary: Indoor-outdoor rooftop bar atop the Mondrian Itaewon, with city views, DJs, single malts and wines by the glass.
description: Privilege sits on the roof of the Mondrian Seoul Itaewon, combining a terrace with a classically styled lounge. It has one of the city's better single-malt selections and a wide list of wines by the glass, and world-class DJs set the soundtrack as the evening goes on. TripAdvisor reviewers highlight the view, the service and the cocktails. It opens at 18:00, so arrive at opening to catch dusk over the city.
highlights: Rooftop terrace with city views
Single malt whisky selection
DJ sets later in the evening
tips: Open 18:00–24:00, and until 02:00 on Fri and Sat. Arrive at 18:00 for sunset (about 18:30 in late September).
Reserve on CatchTable for a terrace table. Weekend nights get loud once the DJ starts, so weekdays suit parents better.
A 16-min walk from Noksapyeong Stn Exit 3; a taxi from home is simpler.

reviews.text: A reviewer calls it the best bar in Itaewon with an amazing view; others praise the service, cocktails and music.
Naver visitors praise the interior, drink range and friendly staff.

name: Seocho Oksang
summary: Wine shop and bar near Gyodae with a rooftop terrace; one of the closest outdoor evening drinks to home.
description: Seocho Oksang ('Seocho Rooftop') pairs a ground-floor wine shop and bar with a rooftop terrace on Seocho-daero, between Gyodae and Seocho stations. The kitchen covers wine-friendly plates such as lamb-rack steak, abalone cream risotto, gambas, charcuterie and pizzas. Locals praise the food and the interior, and Naver marks it group-friendly with valet parking. It is about 12 minutes on foot from home, which makes it an easy low-effort evening for parents.
highlights: Rooftop terrace

name: Liquortation
summary: Design-led Sinsa basement wine bar with a huge list and good music; very limited opening days during the trip.
description: Liquortation is a basement wine bar in the Nonfiction building between Sinsa and Apgujeong. Its drinks list is its calling card (1,290 Naver mentions), closely followed by the interior (1,176). It also works as a bottle shop and a Dailyshot pick-up point. The music and conversation-friendly room make it popular for long evenings. It has more than 2,400 Naver visitor reviews and is marked group-friendly with valet parking.
highlights: Very large wine selection
Design-forward basement room
Good music and conversation-friendly seating
tips: Check the calendar first: closed Mon and Tue, closed 24–26 Sep for Chuseok, and booked for private events on 23 Sep. During the trip it is realistically open only Sun 27 and Wed 30 Sep, from 18:00.
